releases.title: Discussions, source address, and send errors
highlights: Reddit and Hacker News posts include comments; replies start collapsed.
Kindle files show the original web address under the title.
If Send to Kindle is refused, the reason shows on the page.
changes: Reddit and Hacker News posts include the discussion; replies start collapsed and expand as a thread.
The Kindle file prints the article's original web address under the title.
Back from an article returns to the same page of the list it was opened from.
After the free week, a notice on login offers Subscribe or Close; Close lasts until the next login.
Subscription says to finish checkout on a phone, not the Kindle.
If Send to Kindle is refused, the reason shows in the page, with a link to Kindle settings when that is what is missing.
Hidden images leave an [Image: caption] marker instead of vanishing.
The article list waits until it has been laid out so the first paint is one page, not a jump.
Turning a page no longer prints how many articles were marked read.
Accounts from before charging began keep sending to Kindle.

releases.title: Easier to follow the news
highlights: Quick start offers newspapers such as BBC, The Guardian, NPR, Tagesschau, and Der Spiegel.
Follow a site by pasting its normal address — no special news link needed.
Send a page to Kindle uses plain language instead of technical terms.
changes: Quick start suggests general newspapers instead of developer sites.
Adding a site asks for a website address and explains that a normal homepage is enough.
Paste an article link to send a page to Kindle; it lands in the library like a book.
If a site cannot be followed, the message says so in plain language.
A feed that fails to update says we will try again, without a technical error dump.

releases.title: Settings pages, Mark read, and your data
highlights: Settings is a list of pages so a Kindle only opens the topic it needs.
Mark a whole feed as read from the category list.
Download or delete everything we hold about the account.
changes: Settings is split into Kindle, Reading, Account, Subscription, Changelog, and Your data.
Your data lets you download a JSON export. Deleting the account removes feeds and articles.
A feed address typed without https:// is accepted.
Until a Kindle address is saved, the Feeds page says where Amazon lists it and how to approve the Extrablatt sender.
From a category, Mark read marks every unread article in that feed.
The article list uses one filter row and fills the screen; the last page of a batch says Mark read and load more.
Imprint, privacy, terms, and withdrawal pages are linked from the footer.

releases.title: Paid plan and a free week
highlights: New accounts get a week of the full plan at no charge.
Supporter is €2.99 a month billed yearly, or €3.99 a month, including VAT.
changes: A new account includes seven days of the full Supporter plan, with no card required.
After that week, reading in the browser stays free; sending to Kindle and adding feeds needs a subscription.
The paid plan is €2.99 a month billed as €35.88 once for 12 months, or €3.99 a month, including VAT. Accounts from before charging began stay free.

releases.title: New send-from address
highlights: Articles and account mail now come from mail@extrablatt.app, labelled Extrablatt.
changes: The shared sender is mail@extrablatt.app instead of a Kindle-branded address. Add that address to Amazon's Approved Personal Document E-mail List or new deliveries will not arrive.

releases.title: Changelog, reading preference, and what's new
highlights: Settings now includes a changelog of recent changes.
After a new release, a short notice highlights what changed.
Marking articles read when you turn the page is a Settings choice.
changes: A changelog in Settings lists recent changes; a popup highlights the most important ones after each new release.
Marking articles as read when you go to the next page can be turned off in Settings. When it is off, new feed articles arrive already marked read so a refresh does not fill Unread with a backlog.
The Older articles list is gone; paging through Articles is the way to go further back.
A category can be renamed even when the new name only differs in capitalization.
The top Refresh button is gone. Feeds still refresh in the background when you open Feeds or Articles, and on the usual schedule.

releases.title: Paste a URL, categories, and e-reader reading
highlights: Send any web page to Kindle by pasting its address on Feeds.
Organize feeds in categories, including renaming a category at once.
Page-at-a-time reading is sized for e-ink screens.
changes: Paste any article URL from Feeds: the page is extracted, stored, and emailed to Kindle like a feed article.
Give feeds a category when adding them, browse by category, and rename a category to move every feed in it.
Page-at-a-time reading and list paging are sized to the device screen so Kindle page turns stay snappy.
Less common article actions sit under More so the reading toolbar stays on one row on small screens.

releases.title: Newsletters and keeping the servers running
highlights: Subscribe to e-mail newsletters with one inbox address per account.
A donation reminder appears every so often after Send-to-Kindle.
changes: Each account can have a newsletter inbox address. Issues show up as articles and send to Kindle like anything else.
A donation link lives in Settings, and a short reminder can appear after every tenth article sent. The app stays free and ad-free either way.
Administrators can see usage telemetry and per-account send limits from Settings.
